audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer reads Akshan x5 then Ekko x2, matching packet.levelChart. Also whys[4] said the lane 'flips to him' at level 6, but win[4] is Akshan — the row and its reason contradicted each other.
audit.why: 52.79% over 1453 games. Akshan holds lane through level 6 because Ekko's 22-second Parallel Convergence is dodgeable and Phase Dive only reaches 325; the flip is the first-item burst spike, which is exactly where win[5] turns.
audit.corrected: Full sides set Akshan x5 then Ekko x2. whys[4] rewritten to explain why Akshan still holds level 6 rather than claiming a flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why is garbled ('Avengerang... no —') and calls Akshan's R 'Vengeance'. The first-item spike is described only as 'a stun-into-one-shot combo' without saying what sets it up.
audit.why: Akshan's R is Comeuppance. Ekko's Chronobreak is 110/80/50s — the rank-1 110 seconds is a long, trackable window, and the first-item spike is real: W stun into Timewinder plus Chronobreak damage on arrival.
audit.corrected: Level 6 phase rewritten around the actual level-6 interaction: your execute exists, but his rewind dodges it. Spike text names the Convergence stun as the enabler.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Chronobreak a 'reset' in five places — 'free reset/escape', 'reset-capable escape', 'escape or reset for free', 'Chronobreak reset', 'stun-and-reset kit'. Chronobreak is not a reset. It makes Ekko untargetable, rewinds him to his position a few seconds ago, and heals him for a percentage of the damage he took in that window.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and the page never states it: Comeuppance stores bullets and then fires them — Chronobreak's untargetable window eats the execute outright. The correct sequencing is to fire after the rewind resolves, not into it. Second consequence, flagged in missingInteractions: because the heal scales off damage received, Grievous Wounds directly cuts the value of his ultimate, which no field mentioned.
audit.corrected: Reset language removed. Untargetability stated as the reason to delay the execute, and anti-heal promoted into breakdown.feeding and the late paragraph. Also carried the missingInteractions dash point: hold Heroic Swing for his Phase Dive engage rather than spending it on poke, and read the E wind-up (it is an auto-attack reset) as the tell.
sources: enemyKit R text ('becoming untargetable and rewinding', 'heals for a percentage of the damage received')

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flags 'Chronobreak' and 'Parallel Convergence' as probable wrong names. Both are Ekko's real ability names. False positives — no edits made on that basis.

edits.before: Avengerang... no — R online: Vengeance executes the chipped from two screens. Chip, then channel.
edits.after: R online: Comeuppance executes the chipped, but Chronobreak's untargetable window eats it.

edits.after: Ekko wins by stunning you inside Parallel Convergence, then rewinding out of your execute untargetable on Chronobreak.

edits.before: Ahead, bully harder: string Ekko off every contact, swing-roam the rivers, and execute the map's mistakes with R.
edits.after: Ahead, punish the 22-second Parallel Convergence: with the anomaly down he has no stun, and Phase Dive only reaches 325.

edits.after: Carry by holding the execute: Chronobreak turns him untargetable mid-rewind, so fire Comeuppance once he has landed, never into it.

edits.before: If Ekko opens the score, reset expectations and respect Chronobreak doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q strings and stay relevant through R executes.
edits.after: If Ekko opens the score, buy Grievous Wounds early — Chronobreak heals off the damage he just took, and uncut it undoes your whole trade. Farm at 850 and bank the swing for his dive.

edits.before: Chronobreak's reset/escape and burst potential let Ekko turn all-ins around, flips to him
edits.after: Comeuppance and the passive shield still edge him at 6 if you dodge the Convergence anomaly

edits.before: His item spike enables a stun-into-one-shot combo that outdamages Akshan, still Ekko favoured
edits.after: His item spike turns the Convergence stun into a burst combo that outdamages Akshan, flips to him

edits.before: Ekko's teamfight stun-and-reset kit gives him the late-game edge over Akshan
edits.after: Ekko's stun plus the untargetable Chronobreak rewind gives him the late edge

edits.before: Chronobreak gives him a free reset/escape and damage burst that swings all-ins his way once you're both near full combos — respect his ult timer before diving.
edits.after: Chronobreak is not a reset — it makes him untargetable, rewinds him to safety and heals off the damage he took, so hold your execute until it has been spent.

edits.before: Ekko's teamfight combo of Convergence stun plus AoE burst plus Chronobreak reset makes him a premier late threat, and unless you isolate him early with R, group fights favor him.
edits.after: Ekko's teamfight combo of Convergence stun plus AoE burst plus an untargetable Chronobreak exit makes him a premier late threat, and unless you isolate him with R, group fights favour him.

edits.before: You still hold the edge through level 5 as long as you're dodging his zone placement and punishing Timewinder misses, but respect that Chronobreak comes online at 6 and gives him a reset-capable escape or burst tool. From this point his all-in threat rises fast if he lands his stun — track his cooldowns closely before committing to extended trades.
edits.after: You still hold the edge through level 5 as long as you dodge his anomaly placement and punish Timewinder misses, but Chronobreak comes online at 6 and turns him untargetable while it rewinds him — it will swallow a badly timed Comeuppance. From here his all-in threat rises fast if he lands the stun, so track the 22-second Convergence before you commit.

edits.before: Once he's fully itemized, Ekko's stun-into-burst combo one-shots squishies and Chronobreak lets him escape or reset for free, making teamfights swing hard in his favor if he catches you in his zone. Your best answer is hunting him down with R while he's split from his team, since a fully-set-up Ekko in a 5v5 is very hard to punish safely.
edits.after: Once he's fully itemized, Ekko's stun-into-burst combo one-shots squishies and Chronobreak rewinds him out untargetable while healing off the damage he took, so teamfights swing hard his way if he catches you in the anomaly. Hunt him with R while he is split from his team, and carry Grievous Wounds — a set-up Ekko is very hard to punish.

edits.before: Use Chronobreak for escape, reset, or damage swing
edits.after: Use Chronobreak to rewind out untargetable and heal

notes: The page described Chronobreak as a 'reset' in five separate fields. It is not a reset — it is an untargetable rewind that heals off damage received. That mistake hid the two interactions that actually decide this matchup: Comeuppance is wasted if fired into the untargetable window, and Grievous Wounds directly cuts the ultimate's heal. Both are now stated. whys[4] also contradicted its own row (said the lane flips to Ekko at 6 while win[4] reads Akshan); rewritten to agree. packet.suspectNames flagged 'Chronobreak' and 'Parallel Convergence' as wrong names — both correct, false positives. Full-layer chart was unset on all seven rows; proposed as one atomic group, content side already matched the packet. Left breakdown.wave and breakdown.mid templated: nothing in Ekko's kit gives a wave-specific interaction I could ground without inventing one. | COHERENCE: 2 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
